target_customer: New York City consumers ordering premium multicourse dinner kits for a special evening at home, and partner fine dining restaurants selling through the marketplace
problem: Restaurants hit by the pandemic needed new revenue, and diners wanted restaurant quality dinners at home without hours of cooking or ordinary takeout.
business_model: Marketplace taking a margin on dinner kits from partner restaurants, priced roughly 60 to 100 dollars per person

founders.name: Jeff Chen
founders.background_notes: Later founded Redcar, an AI sales rep company, per the YC page.

founders.name: Daryl Sew
founders.background_notes: Later cofounder and CTO of Certainly Health. Has worked on self driving cars.

competitors.name: Goldbelly
competitors.what: Marketplace shipping food from iconic restaurants nationwide
competitors.traction_then: 850 restaurant partners across all 50 states in May 2021
competitors.funding_then: 100 million dollar Series C announced May 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: A storefront plus logistics coordination. The hard parts were cold chain packaging, scheduled restaurant pickups two days ahead and delivery operations, which are operational rather than technical.

defensibility.rationale: Restaurant relationships were non exclusive and the kits were copyable by restaurants themselves or by Goldbelly. Little data or network effect.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Goldbelly raised 100 million dollars in May 2021 for national restaurant e commerce, and restaurants reopened as pandemic restrictions ended. No source shows an acquisition of Taste.

market_need_then: In early 2021 pandemic restrictions had New York restaurants searching for delivery revenue and consumers were spending on at home dining. TechCrunch reported 16 Michelin starred or rated restaurants on the platform at launch in February 2021.

branding.domain_note: Uses gettaste.com, a prefixed domain rather than taste.com, per the YC listing. The site could not be fetched.

identity.visual_style: Premium packaging with a large outer box, separate course packages and a spice packet
identity.voice_and_tone: Aspirational. The founder pitched it as the Instagram of nice food

branding.brand_signature: Pitch as an Instagram for nice food, with extras like a Spotify playlist in the box
branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch launch coverage in February 2021 and a Product Hunt listing from 26 January 2021.

brand_strength.rationale: Some launch press and premium restaurant partners, but the name is a very common word that now collides with other companies called Taste, and no lasting brand evidence was found.

outcome_analysis: Taste launched in New York in February 2021 with Michelin rated partners and kits costing 60 to 100 dollars per person. The cause of its shutdown is not public. The likely pressures, which are inferences from the model and not sourced statements, are that kit logistics and premium pricing limited the market once restaurants reopened and Goldbelly scaled nationally, while both founders went on to other companies.
notes: The shutdown cause is not public: searches found no post mortem or closure announcement, and the failure factors are inferences labeled as such, so treat them as low confidence. Unverified funding: CB Insights lists a pre seed from 2048 Ventures and Y Combinator, about $130K total, with conflicting dates, from one aggregator, so no round is recorded. The company website did not resolve. Closure date unknown. Goldbelly source is dated two months after the batch.
